title: Dell Technologies Sees AI Boom Building as $95B Server Backlog Signals Demand
excerpt: Michael Dell, CEO and founder of Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL), said enterprises are in the early stages of adopting artificial intelligence infrastructure,...
content_html:
Key Points

  • Interested in Dell Technologies Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

  • Dell's $95 billion AI server backlog—following $130 billion in orders over the past year—signals strong demand, with customers prioritizing product availability amid potentially tighter semiconductor supplies through 2027.

  • Enterprise AI adoption remains in its early stages, but Dell is supporting 6,500 AI Factory customers as companies deploy hybrid and on-premises systems to keep proprietary data closer to operations.

  • Dell expects AI to drive longer-term growth across servers, storage, networking and PCs, while sovereign AI projects, neocloud providers and aging hardware fleets provide additional demand catalysts.

  • MarketBeat Week in Review – 09/07 - 09/11

Michael Dell, CEO and founder of Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL), said enterprises are in the early stages of adopting artificial intelligence infrastructure, with companies increasingly viewing technology spending as a means of creating value rather than as a traditional IT budget expense.

Speaking at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia + Technology Conference, Dell said AI is prompting organizations to rethink business processes, though adoption is progressing at different speeds. He estimated that roughly 10% to 15% of companies understand the strategic importance of AI and are moving to implement it, while many others remain uncertain about how to proceed.

→ 3 Under-$20 Stocks Tied to the Future of U.S. Energy and Materials

  • AI Token Costs Are Changing the Hardware vs. Software Debate

"The real opportunity is reimagining the whole workflows," Dell said. He said companies must simplify and standardize processes, assemble relevant data and then apply AI. While providing employees with AI tools can improve productivity, Dell said broader gains would come from redesigning operations and automating work previously performed by people.

AI Factories and On-Premises Data

Dell said the company has 6,500 enterprise AI Factory customers and is helping organizations deploy AI closer to their proprietary data. He argued that customers in sectors including manufacturing, restaurants, retail and logistics may need AI operating at their facilities rather than solely in centralized cloud environments.

→ Chewy's Sell-Off Puts Its Recurring Revenue Story Back on Trial for Investors

  • NVIDIA's Hugging Face Deal Raises a Bigger Question About Its AI Moat Now

"For your most valuable data, your proprietary data, your hard-fought knowledge that only you have inside your company, you don't want to send that off to somebody else," Dell said.
